title: Automated safety gates and experiment dashboards for batching + KV-prefetch configs
creator: Priya Raman
description: Goal: Build an automated experiment pipeline and dashboarding surface that compares alternative batching and KV-prefetch configurations while enforcing safety gates and automatic rollback when regressions are detected. This ticket covers experiment design, metric instrumentation, automated signal checks, dashboard templates, and an ops playbook for manual override. The target outcome is a repeatable A/B comparison workflow that can safely recommend and apply cost-saving batching/caching configs with minimal human intervention.
acceptance_criteria: A producible experiment spec (JSON) that can deploy two config cohorts: control (current defaults) and treatment (new batching + KV-prefetch settings).
Metrics ingested: cost-per-token, infra-cost-per-minute, p50/p95 latency, SLA-breach-rate, request-failure-rate, downstream error-rate, and throughput (requests/sec).

Automated safety gate engine that evaluates live cohorts every 5 minutes and triggers pause/rollback if: SLA-breach-rate increases by >0.5 percentage points OR p95 latency regresses >30% OR request-failure-rate increases >0.2 percentage points. Thresholds configurable via runtime flags.

Dashboard template (Grafana) with panels for experiment-level metrics, cohort comparison, cumulative lift charts, and a statistical significance panel (bootstrap CIs and sequential p-value visualization).
Alerting rules (Slack + PagerDuty) configured for safety gate trips and when experiment reaches decision boundary (win/loss/inconclusive).
Playbook documented for manual investigation steps and a rollback runbook with links to relevant logs and PRs.
experiment_design: Randomization: hash(user_id) mod 100 -> 0-49 control, 50-99 treatment. For non-user traffic use request_id bucketing with sticky sessions for 24h.

Sample size and MDE: target 95% power, two-sided test. For cost-per-token MDE = 5% default; sample estimation script included in repo. Initial pilot uses 10k requests/minute for 2 hours to sanity-check instrumentation.

Duration and stopping rules: minimum 24h run; sequential monitoring allowed but decision only after minimum sample. Early stop allowed if safety gates trigger. Final decision requires both cost improvement and no quality regressions.
Stratification: split by model family (small/medium/large), request type (generation/streaming/embedding), and region to control confounders. Cohorts balanced per stratum.
metrics_definition: cost-per-token: total infra cost attributed to tokens served divided by token count for cohort (uses cost allocation from billing-metering pipeline).
infra-cost-per-minute: GPU/minutes consumed by cohort normalized to baseline machine types.
p50_latency_ms: median wall-clock from request arrival to token generation start.
p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile end-to-end latency measured at the edge.
sla_breach_rate: fraction of requests with latency > configured SLO for that route.
request_failure_rate: fraction of requests that return 5xx or internal error.
quality_signal_proxy: token-level perplexity delta and heuristic rerank regression count for a seeded prompt set (used as a lightweight quality guard).
stat_significance: bootstrap 95% confidence intervals and sequential p-value; report both uplift and CI lower-bound.
dashboard_panels: Cohort overview: live totals for requests, tokens, infra-cost, and cost-per-token for control vs treatment.
Latency distribution: stacked violin/histograms for p50/p95 with region/model overlays.
Safety Gate Indicators: binary panels showing active safety trips, reason, and time since trip.
Cost lift waterfall: component breakdown (batching efficiency, KV-hit-rate, concurrency changes) explaining cost delta.
Statistical Summary: uplift %, CI, p-value over time, and accumulated sample size.
Quality sentinel dashboard: seeded prompt pass/fail, perplexity trend, and sample outputs for quick manual review.
Infrastructure impact: GPU utilization, avg batch size, queue depth, and autoscaler actions.
rollout_playbook: Pre-flight: run traffic replay with production traces in staging and validate metrics match within 5% of production. Attach replay run artifacts to ticket.
Canary: start with 1% traffic for 15 minutes; if no safety trips, step to 10% for 30 minutes, then 50% for 1 hour, then full roll when stable.

Automated rollback: safety engine will mark treatment as paused and trigger a config rollback action that re-applies the control cohort routing. Notify on Slack and open AUTO-ROLLBACK-{timestamp} ticket.
Manual investigation steps: collect traces (X-Request-ID), inspect KV hit/miss logs, verify batch assembler metrics, and run sample prompt checks from the seeded set.
Post-mortem: if rollback occurs, collect experiment logs, related PRs, and a timeline; schedule a blameless postmortem within 48h.
